snippet: It has been less than four years, since ChatGPT made its public debut, but talk of AI has taken over business, investing and even personal conversations. The AI debate, though, has gone off the tra…
content_text: [1/12 @AswathDamodaran] It has been less than four years, since ChatGPT made its public debut, but talk of AI has taken over business, investing and even personal conversations. The AI debate, though, has gone off the tracks as people talk past each other and distractions about. My attempt to make sense of it all: https://bit.ly/4qqIV30 --- [2/12 @AswathDamodaran] Revolutionary change moves through a cycle from hype & hope to an investing build-up to building businesses to a recalibration. Each phase brings new players and challenges, and AI seems to be entering the business building phase- it's bar mitzvah moment is here. https://bit.ly/4qqIV30 --- [3/12 @AswathDamodaran] The components that go into building a business are universal, and start with an assessment of where revenues will go, what profitability will look like & how much reinvestment will be needed to get to your destination. https://bit.ly/4qqIV30 --- [4/12 @AswathDamodaran] The total market size for AI will depend on whether you think it is tool or employee replacement, whether it will target just high-priced employees or all of them, and its reach across industries and geographies. https://bit.ly/4qqIV30 --- [5/12 @AswathDamodaran] While there is room for disagreement, there are hard limits on how big the AI market can be, with total operating expenses at all companies last year and total wages paid to employees by all businesses as limiting points. https://bit.ly/4qqIV30 --- [6/12 @AswathDamodaran] The profitability of AI products will depend on business models adopted by AI businesses, with usage beating out subscription, and unit economics where lower token cost effects are being offset by token usage in more powerful models. https://bit.ly/4qqIV30 --- [7/12 @AswathDamodaran] AI is creating a backlash because of its real estate footprint, worries about data privacy and job loss and concerns that it will make income inequality worse, and it will show up as restrictions, constraints and taxes for AI businesses. https://bit.ly/4qqIV30 --- [8/12 @AswathDamodaran] If your immediate concern is deciding whether Anthropic is worth $2 trillion (rumored IPO pricing) or whether the hyper scalers will make back their money on $2 trillion plus in cap ex, you can try reverse engineering how much revenue you will need to break even at those prices. https://bit.ly/4qqIV30 --- [9/12 @AswathDamodaran] With Anthropic, allowing for 30% after-tax operating margins and a cost of capital of 10%, you will need $1.2 trillion in revenues if the business matures in ten years and $2 trillion if you have to wait 15 years. https://bit.ly/45G3jUp --- [10/12 @AswathDamodaran] Looking at AI as a consolidated business, and using a melded after-tax operating margin of 20%, you will need $5 trillion in revenues in year 10 to justify a pricing today of $5 trillion and almost $8 trillion if it will take 15 years. https://bit.ly/4hKFy4T --- [11/12 @AswathDamodaran] You can use the linked spreadsheet to back out what you will need in revenues to justify the pricing of any AI company or the cap ex of any hyperscaler. https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/pc/blog/BreakevenEnterprisevalue.xlsx --- [12/12 @AswathDamodaran] I developed this framework to make sense of the AI debate, but I am clear eyed about what it will not and will do. It will not price companies for me or tell me what the TAM for AI is, but I can use it to estimate both. https://bit.ly/4qqIV30
